title: Emergence of Stigmergic Transport in Granular Environments
authors: F. Wéry, F. N. Pinan Basualdo, B. Gorissen, N. Vandewalle
abstract: We show that stigmergic path formation emerges in a deformable environment through the interplay between environmental memory and geometrical crowding. Using experiments with robotic random walkers together with a minimal stochastic model, we demonstrate the onset of persistent self-reinforced transport pathways above a critical packing fraction $φ_c$, where environmental memory enhances walker mobility. As the jamming transition $φ_J$ is approached, increasing crowding progressively suppresses this transport enhancement despite the persistence of environmental memory. The resulting non-monotonic behavior reveals an optimal transport regime well below jamming. More generally, our work establishes how active agents can collectively build transport networks through purely mechanical interactions with a deformable substrate.
summary: This paper demonstrates that active agents can collectively build robust transport networks in granular media through stigmergic interactions. By coupling movement to environmental remodeling, the system exhibits enhanced mobility in an optimal regime that exists well below the jamming limit. The findings provide a general framework for understanding self-organized transport in complex, deformable substrates.
main_problem: The paper investigates the emergence of stigmergic transport—self-organized movement pathways—in deformable, granular environments.
main_result: Stigmergic transport emerges only above a critical packing fraction ($\phi_c$), leading to enhanced mobility, but this enhancement is suppressed as the system approaches the jamming transition ($\phi_J$).
method: The study combines physical experiments using robotic walkers in granular media with a minimal stochastic simulation model.
model_or_system: The system involves active agents (robotic walkers) moving through a deformable substrate of granular material (wooden cubes). The model tracks how movement modifies the local packing fraction ($\phi_i$) of the environment.
key_observables: Average velocity ($\langle v angle$), normalized mobility ($\mu$), and a memory order parameter ($m$) quantifying environmental structuring.
important_parameters: Packing fraction ($\phi$), critical packing fraction ($\phi_c$), and the jamming transition ($\phi_J$).
main_assumptions: The model assumes material displacement is redistributed isotropically among neighbors, allowing for the persistence of depleted regions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the formation of particle traces and robot trajectories at different packing fractions, and plots show the evolution of mobility and the memory order parameter across the different transport regimes.
paper_structure: The work establishes the physical system, defines the competition between environmental memory and geometrical crowding, demonstrates the emergence of three regimes (random, trail formation, narrow path), and quantifies the optimal transport regime before jamming.
why_interesting: The concept of self-organization driven by mechanical interactions and environmental memory is highly relevant to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics, pattern formation, and active matter systems.
